classification.difficultyReason: Form a shared perimeter constraint for two shapes, eliminate one variable, and differentiate and classify the resulting area function.

content.prompt: A piece of wire $10$ m long is broken into $2$ parts, which are bent into the shape of a rectangle and a square as shown. Find the dimensions $x$ and $y$ that make the total area a maximum.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle on the left and square on the right, with aligned top and bottom edges. The rectangle is drawn wider than the square, as in the source; proportions are schematic, not additional givens. Ordinary source grey outlines use house black.
spec.mathematics: The rectangle has horizontal side y and vertical side x. The square has side x. Their combined perimeter is 2x + 2y + 4x.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no solution values.

answer.worked:
The total wire length gives
$$\begin{align*}P&=2x+2y+4x\\P&=6x+2y\\10&=6x+2y\\y&=5-3x.\end{align*}$$
Both dimensions must be positive, so $0<x<\frac53$.

The total area is
$$\begin{align*}A&=xy+x^2\\A&=x(5-3x)+x^2\\A&=5x-3x^2+x^2\\A&=5x-2x^2.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A'(x)&=5-4x\\0&=5-4x\\x&=\frac54=1.25.\end{align*}$$
Since $A''(x)=-4<0$ throughout the domain, this gives the maximum total area.
$$\begin{align*}y&=5-3\left(\frac54\right)\\y&=\frac54=1.25.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=1.25\text{ m}$ and $y=1.25\text{ m}$.
